claims.statement: Salesforce's authorizing server grants access tokens to an external client app or connected app under OAuth 2.0, and a resource server validates them before approving access to the protected REST API resource.

sources.supports: In response, an authorizing server grants access tokens to the external client app or connected app.
sources.locator: Authorization Through External Client Apps or Connected Apps and OAuth 2.0: flow steps

claims.statement: Salesforce documents the access token as the access_token parameter of the response of the OAuth 2.0 web server flow token request (token_type Bearer), and its REST API Quick Start sends the access token after Bearer in an Authorization header of REST API requests (the same page calls these OAuth access tokens). Documented for an external client app; a connected app and an external client app token are not distinguished.

sources.supports: access_token OAuth token that an external client app uses to request access to a protected resource on behalf of the client application. Additional permissions in the form of scopes can accompany the access token.
sources.locator: OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow for Web App Integration, token response parameters
Using cURL, Handle Exclamation Marks in Access Tokens

openQuestions.question: This candidate is recorded at existence level only: the pages read state no format for an access token, and do not say how a session-bound access token differs from other Salesforce session identifiers. Is its shape documented, or is it opaque and context-dependent? One open-source scanner rule artifact (TruffleHog, read 2026-10-04) describes an org-identifier-plus-token shape for it; a single artifact does not corroborate, so it stays a lead and no shape is recorded.
The pages read describe one access token for both an external client app and a connected app; whether the token differs by app kind is not stated, so no subtype is recorded.
The pages state no prefix, alphabet or width; the example values on them are not format statements and are not recorded.
